Code §3294 unless the defendant was served with this statutory notice before default is taken, and pleading punitives in the complaint alone does not satisfy §425.115. On August 4, 2026 at 8:00 AM, Plaintiff emailed the completed SER-001, the CCP §425.115 Notice, and the granted FW-003 order to the Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department Civil Process Bureau (csdwebmail@lasd.org), requesting personal service on FedEx's registered agent, Ct Corporation System, at the same Glendale address used for the original summons/complaint service (LASD File No. 2026075280) — no response/confirmation from LASD received as of this writing. This entry will be updated once LASD confirms acceptance and completes service. PUNITIVE AMOUNT REVISED — AUGUST 7, 2026: the August 4, 2026 notice(s) in this action carried a flat $25,000.00 figure copied from Matter 12 (Diamond/Alpine), a ~$53.7K fraud action against a small dealership with no analytical relationship to this defendant. Two defects drove the revision: (1) $25,000 is also the Pen. Code §290.46(j)(4)(A) statutory floor that supplies this action's COMPENSATORY backbone, so noticing punitive damages at the identical figure invited a prove-up court to read the punitive request as duplicative of the statutory penalty; and (2) §425.115 caps punitive damages recoverable ON DEFAULT and cannot be raised once default is entered, making an under-set figure a permanent ceiling in the only scenario the document exists for, while imposing no cap at all if the defendant appears (§425.115(c)). An AMENDED Notice of Amount of Punitive Damages Sought stating $250,000.00 (~3:1 against the ~$80,000 modeled moderate compensatory figure) was executed August 7, 2026, expressly superseding the August 4, 2026 $25,000.00 notice in full, together with a replacement SER-001 directing Los Angeles County Sheriff Civil Process to serve the amended document on Ct Corporation System. NOT YET SUBMITTED. The revised amount is anchored to this matter's modeled compensatory exposure at a ratio inside the single-digit due-process bound of State Farm v. Campbell (2003) 538 U.S. 408 and Simon v. San Paolo U.S. Holding Co. (2005) 35 Cal.4th 1159. An amended statement that raises the amount must itself be served before default is entered — recovery on default is limited to the amount stated in the statement in effect at that time — so the amended notice must reach this defendant before any default is taken to have effect. The August 4, 2026 notice and SER-001 are retained in the file as the record of the superseded statement. CAVEAT — the notice sets a ceiling, it does not supply proof: any punitive award at a default prove-up still requires meaningful evidence of the defendant's financial condition, which Plaintiff bears the burden of producing (Adams v. Murakami (1991) 54 Cal.3d 105).

status: Pre-complaint — 26-page verified Complaint v9 prepared naming Moua and DOES 1-10 only, anticipated filing September 16, 2026 (USDC N.D. Cal.), 15 days after the Government Claims Act claim is deemed rejected; Gary Noguchi and Joseelyn Rojo were served (Jul. 7 and Jul. 14, 2026) under an earlier complaint draft naming them directly, but Plaintiff has since deliberately narrowed the operative pleading to Moua alone, reserving them for potential later DOE amendment; Long Moua service pending; Government Claims Act claim filed Jul. 18, 2026, anticipated deemed-rejected Sep. 1, 2026 (Gov. Code §912.4(c)); plaintiff homeless since Jul. 2, 2026. MACY'S EMPLOYMENT FORMALLY TERMINATED BY RESIGNATION JULY 31, 2026: what had been an open-ended medical Leave of Absence (preferred return date August 12, 2026) is now a completed, irreversible job loss — BNN texted Macy's manager Lety Villarreal on Friday, July 31, 2026 at 10:42 AM resigning effective immediately, citing the Santa Clara parole transfer making the Stockton commute impossible; Lety accepted the resignation at 10:45 AM. This converts the damages theory from an interrupted/paused employment to a permanent termination directly and expressly attributed by BNN, in writing, to the retaliatory transfer — strengthening the causal chain for both the §1983 retaliation claim and the lost-wages component of damages.
note: NOT abandoned — if discharged from CDCR parole supervision before this matter's filing window closes, Plaintiff intends to file it.
defendants: Long Moua (CDCR Parole Agent, Badge #7472 — received BNN's file on or about Jan. 26, 2026, ~14 days after BNN filed the Derrick FAC; fabricated March 31, 2026 telehealth 'failure to attend treatment' violation by withholding the access code then submitting BNN's non-attendance as willful; authored Nov. 14, 2025 CDCR Form 1502-DR (Discharge Review Report), reviewed/e-signed by Noguchi, judicially questioned by Sacramento County Superior Court; ordered retaliatory transfer to Santa Clara GPS Unit on Jun. 29, 2026, 7 days after BNN served CDCR in separate lawsuit, citing 'too many violations'); and DOES 1–10, inclusive. NOTE: an earlier complaint draft named Gary Noguchi (CDCR Parole Agent, Badge #7284, Unit Supervisor San Joaquin County Parole GPS Unit — Moua's direct supervisor; co-defendant in Newanforbi v. Andrew Derrick et al. FAC, Case 2:26-cv-00004-DJC-JDP; co-authored the 1502-DR with Moua) and Joseelyn Rojo (CDCR Parole official) as co-defendants, and both were served under that draft (Noguchi Jul. 7, 2026; Rojo Jul. 14, 2026). Plaintiff has confirmed the narrowing to Moua-only in the operative Complaint v9 was a deliberate strategic choice, not an oversight — the claim against Moua is pleaded on its own facts, with Noguchi and Rojo reserved for potential later amendment as DOE defendants if discovery substantiates their supervisory involvement. FLAGGED RISK FOR THAT RESERVATION: Matter 3's July 24, 2026 order already dismissed a supervisory-liability theory against this same Noguchi 'for lack of supervisory-liability allegations under Hansen v. Black' (with leave to amend, not a final merits adjudication — and in the same order the court itself noted this sits in tension with Plaintiff's own July 22, 2026 self-executing voluntary dismissal of Noguchi from that action). Neither ruling forecloses a differently-pleaded supervisory theory here, but any future DOE amendment naming Noguchi should address Hansen v. Black head-on rather than repeat the pleading gap Matter 3 already identified. This matter also does not currently disclose its overlap with the discharge-review cluster (Matters 9, 10, 11, 15, 19) — Moua co-authored the same Nov. 14, 2025 Form 1502-DR whose facial defects are the entire subject of that cluster (see Matter 19, now the sole still-pending vehicle for that challenge). Separately, this matter's causal account of the June 29, 2026 retaliatory transfer (Moua's personal decision, driven by the fabricated telehealth violation) differs from Matters 3 and 15's account of the same transfer (institutional retaliation by 'Stockton parole,' Noguchi's unit, tied to the Matter 15 filing) — the two framings aren't mutually exclusive, but neither cross-references the other, and a factfinder crediting one causal story could undercut the other.
causes: 42 U.S.C. § 1983 — First Amendment Retaliation: Moua received BNN's file within ~14 days of the Derrick lawsuit (Jan. 12 → Jan. 26, 2026); Moua executed retaliatory transfer to Santa Clara GPS Unit within 18 days of CDCR lawsuit service (Jun. 22 → Jun. 29, 2026); causal nexus between protected petition activity and adverse parole action established by temporal proximity and Moua's cited pretext ('too many violations')

42 U.S.C. § 1983 — Fourteenth Amendment Due Process: fabricated 'failure to attend treatment' violation submitted by Moua into the parole system based on a telehealth session BNN could not attend because Moua never provided the access code; manufactured pretext used to justify retaliatory transfer without legitimate administrative basis

Tom Bane Civil Rights Act, Cal. Civ. Code § 52.1 — coercive interference with First and Fourteenth Amendment rights: Moua's use of the fabricated violation as a threatened and actual sanction (administrative record blemish + retaliatory transfer) constitutes threats, intimidation, and coercion within the meaning of §52.1; third-strike sex offender registration completed under duress of automatic life sentence amplifies the coercive context

Intentional Infliction of Emotional Distress: fabrication of a parole violation, forced relocation from Stockton to Santa Clara GPS jurisdiction, destruction of Macy's employment ($21.50/hr Captain role, ~$3,870+ lost wages), compelled sex offender registration under duress of third-strike life sentence, and ongoing housing and employment instability constitute extreme and outrageous conduct causing severe emotional distress

[RESERVED — not pleaded in operative Complaint v9] Supervisory Liability (42 U.S.C. § 1983) as to Noguchi and Rojo: a prior complaint draft alleged supervisory defendants ratified, condoned, or failed to prevent Moua's retaliatory conduct, and both were served under that draft (Jul. 7 and Jul. 14, 2026); Plaintiff deliberately narrowed the operative pleading to Moua alone, preserving this theory as a potential DOE amendment rather than pleading it in the five-count complaint prepared for filing

caption: Newanforbi v. First Advantage LLC
claims: FCRA § 1681b(b), FCRA § 1681e(b), ICRAA, Negligence Per Se, UCL § 17200
status: IDENTIFIED VIA PORTFOLIO GAP ANALYSIS (Jul. 30, 2026) — NOT YET FILED; no demand letter sent; no complaint drafted. Opened as a candidate matter after a document-level review found First Advantage LLC named as the background-check vendor in both Matter 25 (FedEx) and Matter 26 (UPS), yet never itself named as a defendant, unlike the comparable vendors in the same cluster (Accurate Background — Matter 29; HireRight — Matter 23).
note: Vendor-side companion to Matters 25/26 — same underlying reports, different defendant theory
defendants: First Advantage LLC (fadv.com; consumer reporting agency / investigative consumer reporting agency); DOES 1 through 10, inclusive
causes: Violation of the Fair Credit Reporting Act, 15 U.S.C. § 1681b(b)(1) — Furnishing a Consumer Report for Employment Purposes Without a Permissible/Certified Purpose
Violation of the Fair Credit Reporting Act, 15 U.S.C. § 1681e(b) — Failure to Follow Reasonable Procedures to Assure Maximum Possible Accuracy
Violation of the California Investigative Consumer Reporting Agencies Act (Cal. Civ. Code § 1786 et seq.)
Negligence Per Se (Evid. Code § 669; predicate duty: Cal. Penal Code § 290.46(j)(2)(E))
Unlawful Business Practices (Bus. & Prof. Code § 17200 et seq.)
